 News Will examine whether case on private university audit needs to continue: Supreme Court after Bench change 
 A Bench led by Justice Amanullah had earlier expanded the scope of the PIL and ordered an audit of private universities across India. The case was recently shifted to a new Bench led by Justice Vikram Nath. Supreme Court of India AI Ritwik Choudhury Published on :  19 Nov 2026, 9:42 am 3 min read 
 Copied 
 Follow Us Listen to this article The Supreme Court on Thursday indicated that it will examine in January whether to continue hearing the public interest litigation (PIL) in which a Bench led by Justice  Ahsanuddin Amanullah  had earlier issued sweeping directions for the audit of private universities across India [ Ayesha Jain v. Amity University Noida & Ors ].
 The development comes days after the case was shifted from the Justice Amanullah bench to a three-judge bench comprising Justice  Vikram Nath ,   R Mahadevan and  Aparesh Kumar Singh .
 "What we propose is we fix the matter for January. We will consider the grievance of the petitioner, subject to report of Mr. Prasad (Mr. Ashok Prasad, who had been tasked with enquiring into certain allegations made by the petitioner regarding Amity University). University has already filed its counter. We will decide then what is the scope of the PIL. Whether to continue it further or not, " the new bench said today.
 The Court then proceeded to adjourn the case till January 2027.
 "Let this matter be listed on Jan 11. The further issues raised in this matter would be considered on the next date... We will consider whether to entertain this petition or not or how far we will carry this , " today's order records. 
 Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The case before the Court originally began in mid-2025 as an individual grievance filed by 23-year-old student Ayesha Jain against Amity University, Noida. Jain alleged that University officials harassed her, barred her from classes and caused her to lose an academic year after she legally changed her name from Khushi Jain to Ayesha Jain.
 While the Bench pulled up Amity's top officials over their treatment of the student, it refused to close the matter after granting her relief. 
 Instead, in November 2025, A Bench of Justices Amanullah and NV Anjaria expanded the scope of the petition in the larger public interest to scrutinise how private universities across India are established, funded and regulated.
 Over the course of multiple hearings, the Bench issued a string of far-reaching directives, including those to furnish details of how private universities are set up and governed, directions to curb profiteering and measures to crack down on fake colleges . 
 The Justice Amanullah-led Bench heard the matter last on October 9, when it was directed to be listed next on November 19.
 However, the matter was recently shifted to the Justice Nath-led Bench, with no reasons being disclosed on the judicial record for the sudden change of bench just days ahead of today's hearing. 
 The development was particularly notable given how aggressively the Justice Amanullah bench had expanded and monitored the present proceedings over the past year.
 In today's hearing before the new Bench, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) KM Nataraj told the Court, 
 " Individual issue of petitioner (Ayesha Jain) has come to an end. Only a report is to be submitted." 
 An amicus curiae present in Court also made a similar submission,
 " The writ petition has become infructuous now. The prayers have been allowed." 
 The ASG, however, also appraised the new Bench that after the PIL's scope was expanded, various States have filed several reports in response to the Court's earlier directions. 
 Meanwhile, petitioner Ayesha Jain told the Court that she wanted new legal representation, since her legal aid counsel had withheld information regarding the case from her and did not appraise the Court of all the facts. The Court agreed to examine Jain's request, albeit in the next hearing.
 " This case only came to us during yesterday evening. We will consider all your submissions on the next date. By the next date we will also be more equipped with the proceedings," the Bench said.
